sources: National Park Service, Yellowstone, Safety in the Park: bison 'have injured more people in Yellowstone than any other animal'; can run 3x faster than humans; keep at least 25 yards (23 m) away; warning signs include bluff charging, head bobbing, pawing, bellowing or raising its tail; https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm

National Park Service, Yellowstone, Bison: largest land mammal in North America; bulls up to 2,000 lb; can run 35 mph; can clear obstacles about 5 ft high; the hump is large muscles on long vertebrae, used to swing the head like a snowplow; wallowing deters biting flies, removes molted fur and leaves scent, bulls wallow in the rut to show strength; 30-60 million bison before the mid-1800s, Yellowstone herd fell to about two dozen by 1902; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/bison.htm

U.S. Department of the Interior, 15 Facts About Our National Mammal: the American Bison: national mammal since May 9, 2016; bulls about 2,000 lb and 6 ft tall; run up to 35 mph, spin quickly, jump high fences; tail hanging down and swishing usually means calm, tail straight up can signal a charge; poor eyesight, excellent smell and hearing; calves born orange-red ('red dogs'); https://www.doi.gov/blog/15-facts-about-our-national-mammal-american-bison

beats.say: The animal most likely to hurt you in Yellowstone isn't a bear. It's this.
The American bison. The biggest land animal in North America.
A bull can weigh two thousand pounds, and stand six feet tall.
It looks slow and sleepy, munching grass all day.
But it can run thirty five miles an hour. Three times faster than you.
It just stands there, chewing. Until it doesn't.
